statement_en: Let V be the set of odd natural numbers that cannot be written as a power of 2 plus a prime. Show that V is not the union of an infinite arithmetic progression {b + m·e : m ∈ ℕ} (with e > 0) and a set C of density zero.
statement_lean:
-- IMPORTS: Mathlib.Data.Set.Card
-- IMPORTS: Mathlib.Analysis.SpecificLimits.Basic
-- IMPORTS: Mathlib.NumberTheory.LSeries.PrimesInAP
theorem erdos_45592
    (V : Set ℕ)
    (hV : V = {n : ℕ | Odd n ∧ ¬ ∃ (k p : ℕ), p.Prime ∧ n = 2 ^ k + p})
    (b e : ℕ) (he : 0 < e)
    (C : Set ℕ)
    (hC : ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ x : ℕ, N ≤ x →
      ((C ∩ Set.Iic x).ncard : ℝ) ≤ ε * (x : ℝ)) :
    V ≠ Set.range (fun m : ℕ => b + m * e) ∪ C := by
  sorry
